The severed heads of members of the Lampião gang on public display. Pirahnas, Brazil. 1938

"Captain" Virgulino Ferreira da Silva, better known as Lampião, was the most famous bandit leader of the Brazilian Northeast in the 1920s and 1930s. For about 16 years he led his band of cangaceiros, which varied greatly in number from around a dozen to up to a hundred, in a career of large-scale banditry through seven states of Brazil.

Lampião's band attacked small towns and farms, took hostages for ransom, extorted money by threats of violence, tortured, fire-branded, and maimed. It has been claimed that they killed over 1,000 people and 5,000 head of cattle and raped over 200 women. The band fought the police over 200 times and Lampião was wounded six times. He was also noted for his loyalty to those he befriended or to whom he owed a debt of gratitude. He generously rewarded his followers and those of the population who shielded or materially helped him (coiteros), and he was entirely reliable if he gave his word of honour.

Lampião was joined in 1930 by his girlfriend, Maria Bonita, which gave his reputation some of the 'romance and violence' notoriety enjoyed in the USA by Bonnie and Clyde.

On July 28, 1938, Lampião and his band were betrayed by one of his supporters and were ambushed in one of his hideouts. A police troop armed with machine guns, killed Lampião, Maria Bonita and nine others and some forty other members of the bandit group managed to escape. The heads of those killed were put on display and, in the image posted, you can see the head of Lampião on the lowest level and that of Maria Bonita immediately above his.
